title: Powerfleet Launches AI-Powered SafeGuard to Help Australian Operators Predict and Prevent Driver Risk With Advanced AI Video Intelligence
summary: Real-time risk management solution helps Australian on-road safety teams proactively identify high-risk driver behaviour and focus attention where…...
body_text: Powerfleet Launches AI-Powered SafeGuard to Help Australian Operators Predict and Prevent Driver Risk With Advanced AI Video Intelligence July 01, 2026 3:00pm EDT Download as PDF Real-time risk management solution helps Australian on-road safety teams proactively identify high-risk driver behaviour and focus attention where it matters most PERTH, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Powerfleet, a global leader in AIoT software-as-a-service (SaaS) solutions for mobile asset management, today announced the Australian launch of SafeGuard, an AI-powered risk intelligence solution designed to help operators identify, prioritise and address high-risk on-road driver behaviour in real time. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260624116649/en/ A fleet safety manager monitors driver risk in real time using SafeGuard, Powerfleet's AI-powered risk intelligence solution now available to Australian fleets. Available as an add-on to Powerfleet's VisionAI video solution and fully integrated within the Unity platform, SafeGuard uses artificial intelligence to continuously assess driver risk across a fleet, helping safety teams focus on the events and behaviours most likely to lead to incidents. The launch comes as Australian operators face increasing pressure to strengthen safety performance and demonstrate proactive risk management under evolving Work Health and Safety (WHS) and Chain of Responsibility obligations. Moving on-road safety from reactive to proactive "Operators have access to more safety data than ever before, but knowing where to focus remains a significant challenge," said Brodie von Berg, Managing Director, Powerfleet APAC. "SafeGuard helps safety teams augment AI video safety by identifying the highest-risk drivers and behaviours in real time, enabling earlier intervention, more effective coaching and ultimately safer outcomes across the fleet." Embedded within the Unity platform, SafeGuard combines real-time risk monitoring, AI-powered real-time driving risk analysis, intelligent video event review and live intervention capabilities to give safety managers greater visibility and control over fleet risk. Operators using SafeGuard have reported up to 83% reduction in on-road risk, 95% fewer false positive video event alerts, and an 80% reduction in video review time, helping safety teams improve operational efficiency while reducing risk. Availability SafeGuard is available now to Australian fleets as an add-on to VisionAI. For more information or to book a demonstration, visit www.powerfleet.com/au/safeguard . About Powerfleet Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR; TASE: PWFL) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonisation and integration of data, irrespective of source, delivering actionable insights that help organisations save lives, time and money. Headquartered in New Jersey, United States, Powerfleet operates globally, serving customers across transportation, logistics, industrial and enterprise markets. For more information, visit www.powerfleet.com View source version on businesswire.com: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260624116649/en/ Australia media contact: Sarah Mead – Marketing Manager, Powerfleet Australia Sarah.Mead@powerfleet.com Source: Powerfleet Released July 1, 2026

title: Union Pacific Corporation Announces 3% Dividend Increase for Third Quarter 2026
summary: Union Pacific Corporation announced that its Board of Directors today voted to increase the quarterly dividend on the Company’s common shares by 3% to $1.42 per share. The dividend is payable September 30, 2026, to shareholders of record August 31, 2026.
body_text: Union Pacific Corporation (NYSE: UNP) announced that its Board of Directors today voted to increase the quarterly dividend on the Company’s common shares by 3% to $1.42 per share. The dividend is payable September 30, 2026, to shareholders of record August 31, 2026. Union Pacific has paid dividends on its common stock for 127 consecutive years. “Union Pacific remains committed to delivering strong financial results and long-term value for our shareholders,” said Jennifer Hamann, executive vice president and chief financial officer. “Today’s announcement reflects that commitment and extends our track record to 20 consecutive years of increased annual dividends per share.” About Union Pacific Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) delivers the goods families and businesses use every day with safe, reliable and efficient service. Operating in 23 western states, the company connects its customers and communities to the global economy. Trains are the most environmentally responsible way to move freight, helping Union Pacific protect future generations. More information about Union Pacific is available at www.up.com . title: Introducing Interactive Maps
summary: New interactive and customizable map components, with powerful filtering features
body_text: Introducing Interactive Maps Sean Hughes May 22nd, 2024 · 3 min read Our community has been eagerly awaiting the addition of maps to the Evidence component library. Today we’re thrilled to share the launch of 4 new interactive map types. These are our most customizable components to date, letting you define custom tooltips, basemaps, and color palettes - among other options. These maps also include interactive features for cross-filtering and drill-down links, making it possible to build highly interactive and intuitive data apps. As always, these components are designed to work well across all device sizes, from mobile phones to ultrawide monitors. This is an exciting step forward for our visualization library and we’re looking forward to seeing what people build. AreaMap Easily create custom choropleth maps with the AreaMap component. Display regions from a geoJSON file, apply a color scale, and add interactivity. AreaMap can accept a local geoJSON (stored in your project’s static folder) or a geoJSON URL. PointMap Use PointMap to display points of interest - great for visualizing things like store locations. PointMaps can be created with the same color across all points, or using a color scale defined by a value column in your query. BubbleMap BubbleMap is similar to PointMap, but with the ability to pass a size column to generate bubble sizes defined by your data. BaseMap BaseMap lets you combine multiple map layers into a single map. Bubbles on top of areas, points inside of bubbles - whatever you need to display. BaseMap’s composable syntax makes it possible to include as many layers as you need, each with their own style and interactivity settings. Interactive Features Maps as Inputs After launching input components in our Universal SQL release , we’re continuing to expand the use cases for inputs across our component library. The maps we’re launching today can be used as inputs - they take a user’s selection and make it accessible as an input variable, which you can use to filter SQL queries on your page. All you need to do is give each map a name , and when your user clicks a point or area on the map, an input variable will get created with the values for that specific point. The input variable will have access to all the columns in the underlying query, so you can choose a specific column when referencing the variable in your SQL (e.g., ${inputs.my_map_name.column_to_use} ) Interactive example → Drill-down Links You can also create drill-down paths for your users to follow by including a link column in your map. When a user clicks an area or point on the map, they’ll automatically navigate to the URL defined in that column. When combined with templated pages , this is great for creating multi-layered drill paths - e.g., drilling from region to state to county. Custom Styling Customizable Color Palettes Use the colorPalette option to supply your own colors to a map’s color scale. You also have control over other visual elements in the chart, including border width/color and opacity: Customizable Tooltips Create custom tooltips with the tooltip option, where you can pass in a list of columns and the formatting/styling you’d like to use for each - including links. Tooltips also include fieldClass and valueClass variables, which allow you to include custom styling (using Tailwind classes), offering almost unlimited customization. Customizable Base Layers Override the basemap layer using the basemap option, which accepts a URL to a tile basemap. If you have a custom basemap you’ve created in a platform like Mapbox, you can use that as well. Coming Soon: More Interactivity Stay tuned for updates as we continue to roll out the input and drill-down link features to the rest of the components in the visualization library. Get started with maps in Evidence We’re excited to see what you build with these maps. Check out the docs for interactive examples or get started with an Evidence project here . If you have questions or feedback, reach out in the Evidence community

title: Managing eConsent in Clinical Trials: A Modern Approach
body_text: In today’s fast-paced clinical trial environment, electronic informed consent (eConsent) is revolutionizing how participants are informed and engaged. This digital transformation replaces traditional paper-based processes, using multimedia tools like videos and quizzes to ensure participants fully understand trial details, from procedures to potential risks and benefits. With eConsent, pharmaceutical companies and contract research organizations (CROs) can enhance patient engagement, improve data accuracy, and ensure regulatory compliance more efficiently. Navigating Challenges with eConsent While eConsent offers numerous benefits, its implementation presents challenges: Regulatory Compliance : One of the most significant challenges is ensuring that eConsent processes comply with global regulatory standards such as the FDA, EMA, and local regulatory bodies. Variations in consent requirements across jurisdictions necessitate a flexible and adaptable eConsent solution that can cater to multiple regulatory environments. Technology Integration : Integrating eConsent platforms with existing clinical trial management systems (CTMS), electronic data capture (EDC) systems, and electronic health records (EHR) can be complex. A lack of seamless integration can result in data silos, inefficiencies, and potential data discrepancies. Data Security and Privacy : Protecting patient data is a critical concern, particularly with the increased use of digital platforms. Ensuring that eConsent platforms comply with data privacy regulations such as GDPR and HIPAA, and implementing robust cybersecurity measures to prevent data breaches, is essential. Patient Accessibility and Digital Literacy : Ensuring that all patients, regardless of their digital literacy or access to technology, can easily navigate and understand the eConsent process is crucial. Organizations must address potential barriers to access, such as language differences, disabilities, and varying levels of comfort with digital tools. User Experience : A poorly designed eConsent platform can hinder patient understanding and engagement. An overly complex or confusing interface may result in incomplete consent forms, lower enrollment rates, and reduced trial retention. Benefits of Using eConsent Despite these challenges, the benefits of eConsent make it a compelling choice for many organizations: Improved Patient Engagement : eConsent platforms use interactive elements such as videos, infographics, and FAQs to make the consent process more engaging and informative. This enhanced understanding leads to greater trust and satisfaction among participants, which can boost recruitment and retention rates. Streamlined Workflows and Reduced Administrative Burden : Automating the consent process reduces the need for paper-based documentation, minimizes manual data entry errors, and streamlines workflows. This efficiency can save time and reduce administrative costs for pharmaceutical companies and CROs. Enhanced Data Accuracy and Integrity : Digital consent forms eliminate the risk of lost or illegible paper documents, ensuring that all consent records are accurately captured, stored, and readily accessible. This improves data integrity and supports audit readiness. Regulatory Adherence and Compliance : eConsent platforms can be configured to automatically ensure compliance with various regulatory requirements, including audit trails, version control, and real-time reporting. This reduces the risk of non-compliance and associated penalties. Best Practices for Managing eConsent To effectively manage eConsent in clinical trials, pharmaceutical companies, and CROs should consider the following best practices: Select the Right eConsent Platform : Choose a platform that integrates seamlessly with existing systems and offers customizable templates to meet specific regulatory requirements. Look for features such as multimedia support, real-time data synchronization, and robust security measures. Ensure Regulatory Compliance : Work closely with legal and regulatory experts to ensure the eConsent process aligns with all relevant regulations. Regularly update consent forms to reflect any changes in regulatory guidelines. Train Staff and Investigators : Provide comprehensive training to clinical trial staff and investigators on using the eConsent platform effectively. This includes understanding how to guide participants through the consent process, troubleshoot technical issues, and maintain data security. Maintain Data Security and Privacy : Implement strong encryption protocols, secure user authentication methods, and regular security audits to protect patient data. Ensure the eConsent platform is compliant with data privacy laws such as GDPR and HIPAA. Prioritize User Experience and Accessibility : Design the eConsent interface to be user-friendly and accessible to all participants, regardless of their digital literacy or physical abilities. Use simple language, provide multi-language options, and offer support for screen readers and other accessibility tools. Looking Ahead: The Future of eConsent Emerging technologies like AI and machine learning are set to further personalize the consent experience, while blockchain promises enhanced data security and transparency. These innovations will continue to transform clinical trials, making eConsent an indispensable tool. Conclusion eConsent is transforming how clinical trials are conducted by improving patient engagement, streamlining workflows, and ensuring regulatory compliance. While challenges remain, the benefits make eConsent an essential tool for pharmaceutical companies and CROs managing high volumes of trials. By adopting best practices and staying ahead of emerging trends, organizations can maximize the potential of eConsent to optimize clinical trial outcomes.
